papers.name: Component 1 20th Century Literature Reading and Creative Prose Writing

topics.name: Section A Reading: unseen 20th-century literary prose extract
points: A1: identifying and listing explicit information from a given section (AO1, 5 marks)
A2: explaining how the writer shows something, with reference to language (AO2, 5 marks)
A3: impressions of a character, place or situation, with textual references (10 marks)
A4: how the writer creates an effect, e.g. tension and drama, through events, language and structure (AO2, 10 marks)
A5: evaluating a statement about the text, with impressions and how the writer creates them (AO4, 10 marks)
Drawing and justifying inferences; identifying themes and ideas
Explaining effects of vocabulary, grammar and structure with accurate terminology

topics.name: Section B Prose writing: narrative or recount
points: One creative task chosen from four titles: narrative or recount (40 marks)
Planning and structuring a narrative for effect; consistent point of view
Using language imaginatively and creatively; creating emotional impact
Communication and organisation (AO5, 24 marks)
Vocabulary, sentence structure, spelling and punctuation (AO6, 16 marks)

papers.name: Component 2 19th and 21st Century Non-Fiction Reading and Transactional/Persuasive Writing

topics.name: Section A Reading: two unseen non-fiction texts (one 19th century, one 21st century)
points: Text types: letters, autobiographies, biographies, diaries, reports, articles, digital and multimodal texts
Short retrieval and interpretation questions (AO1)
Analysing how a writer persuades or creates effects: what is said, language, tone and structure (AO2, 10 marks)
Evaluating a writer's views: thoughts and feelings on what is said and how it is said (AO4, 10 marks)
Synthesising information and ideas from both texts (AO1)
Comparing writers' ideas, perspectives and how they are conveyed across both texts (AO3, 10 marks)
Critical reading: bias, misuse of evidence and reading texts in context

topics.name: Section B Writing: transactional, persuasive and discursive writing
points: Two compulsory writing tasks, each 20 marks (12 AO5, 8 AO6)
Forms: letters, articles, reports, reviews and speeches for different audiences
Writing to argue, persuade, explain and inform; discursive writing
Selecting and emphasising key points; using evidence and quotation; rhetorical devices
Communication and organisation for audience, purpose and form (AO5)
Vocabulary, sentence structure, spelling and punctuation (AO6)

topics.name: Spoken Language endorsement (non-exam assessment)
points: Selecting and organising information and ideas for a prepared formal presentation, agreed in advance with the teacher
Planning for different purposes and audiences; presentation formats (talk, speech, debate or dialogue)
Giving the presentation in a formal setting (up to about ten minutes)
Listening and responding appropriately to questions and feedback
Using spoken Standard English
Pass, Merit and Distinction criteria; graded separately and not part of the 9 to 1 grade
